commercial_incentive: Channel promotes the counselor's own college-counseling practice, though this video itself has no direct sales pitch
key_insights: Recommends deferred or waitlisted students do additional research to find one new, specific reason the college is a great match
Suggests reflecting on what has changed since applying: new grades, accomplishments, or activities not yet known to the college
Advises identifying and emailing the specific regional admissions counselor responsible for the student's geographic area, found on the college's website
Recommends the email state the student still considers the school a top choice and explain the mutual fit
States there are no guarantees and it is generally hard to move from deferral/waitlist to acceptance
Frames success as depending on articulating fit clearly, not just expressing enthusiasm
notable_or_distinctive: Gives a concrete, actionable three-step process (add a new fit reason, note what's changed about you, contact the specific regional rep) rather than vague encouragement.
reliability_notes: Video is 8 years old, so any implied norms about counselor responsiveness or the effectiveness of this tactic may be dated; advice is presented as general practice without citing specific college policies.
